content_voiceover: This case shows a thirty-four year old woman with choriocarcinoma, multiple metastases, and DIC, illustrating acral ischemic necrosis of the fingers and toes, with dark purple-black discoloration of the distal digits and surrounding petechial hemorrhage on the dorsum of the hand and foot. Choriocarcinoma is a gestational trophoblastic malignancy that's highly vascular and prone to both hemorrhage and thromboembolic complications, and when it triggers DIC, patients develop this combination of digital ischemia from microvascular thrombosis alongside petechiae and ecchymoses from the consumptive bleeding diathesis. This case reinforces the malignancy-associated DIC category from the earlier table, and it's a good reminder that gestational trophoblastic disease, though rare, is a boards-favorite cause of DIC in a woman of reproductive age, especially when paired with an elevated beta-hCG and pulmonary or CNS metastases. The digital gangrene pattern here, distinct from the more confluent purpura fulminans on the prior slide, still reflects the same underlying pathophysiology of fibrin thrombus formation in the microvasculature superimposed on a bleeding tendency from factor and platelet consumption.
keypoints: 34F, choriocarcinoma with metastases, complicated by DIC
Digital ischemic necrosis (fingers/toes) + petechiae = combined thrombotic-bleeding DIC picture
Choriocarcinoma: highly vascular gestational trophoblastic tumor, prone to DIC
Consider GTD/choriocarcinoma as a DIC cause in reproductive-age women with high beta-hCG
keypoint_voiceover: This is a thirty-four year old woman with metastatic choriocarcinoma complicated by DIC, showing dark ischemic necrosis of the fingers and toes alongside petechial bleeding. Choriocarcinoma is a highly vascular gestational trophoblastic tumor that can trigger DIC through the same combined thrombotic and consumptive bleeding mechanism seen in other malignancies. Keep gestational trophoblastic disease on your differential for DIC in a reproductive-age woman, particularly with a markedly elevated beta-hCG.
